name: text.template
doc:
Typed text templates with Go text/template syntax: {{.Field.Sub}},
{{$}}, {{$x := pipeline}}, pipelines with | and builtin or custom
functions, {{if}}/{{else if}}/{{else}}, {{range [$i, $e :=] ...}} (with
{{break}}/{{continue}}/{{else}}), {{with}}, {{define}}/{{template}}/
{{block}}, comments {{/* */}} and trim markers {{- -}}.

Parse<T> checks every field path against T: at compile time when the
source is a string literal (sema/litcheck.rs), otherwise at run time
from T's reflection table, so a misspelt field is an error before any
data is rendered. Execute converts the data to a dynamic Value tree
(compile-time reflection) and interprets the template over it. Struct
methods cannot be called (fields only).

html.template uses this engine with contextual escaping: every
action is escaped for where it appears (text, attribute, URL, JS, CSS),
as Go's html/template does (see htmlctx.zl).
